params.body:
Inzichten says how the platform does as a business. Koppelingen says whether every third party
answered this morning. Neither says whether the moving parts still move, and that is what this
screen is for: **Beheer > Werking**, administrator only, read only, one button that empties a
minute of cache and nothing else.

Six sections, in the order the questions get asked:

1. **What wants attention now** — at most four lines, worst first, and on a quiet morning it says
   that everything runs. It is a consequence of the measurements below, never a second truth.
2. **The clock** — every scheduled task with when it last ran, whether that worked, and when it
   was due. The heartbeat separately.
3. **The queue** — a week of failures grouped per job class, with how many, when last, and the
   first line of the error.
4. **The photo mill** — photos without derived sizes, and photos that have carried `processing`
   for more than an hour with the oldest named.
5. **The partner API** — per dealer the calls, how many answered with an error, when the last one
   was, plus the busiest endpoints.
6. **Who is inside** — active in the last quarter of an hour, and per garage when somebody was
   last there, oldest first.
7. **Reported problems** — the messages from the "iets werkt niet"-button.

**Almost all of it was already being measured and nobody looked.** The scheduler writes every
finished task into the cache for Elixir, so "what ran, when, and did it work" needed no new
plumbing. Two choices in there are worth naming. The list of tasks is read from the schedule
itself, not from a list somebody keeps, so a task added to `routes/console.php` appears here by
itself and one that is removed disappears; and "was due" is computed from each task's own cron
expression, so *late* is a comparison rather than a guess. A task nobody has seen run yet is "nog
niet gezien" and not late, because otherwise the first deploy after this paints every row red, and
a screen that is red on arrival is a screen you stop reading.

The heartbeat is asked apart from the tasks, and that is the part that is not obvious: lose the
crontab line and every task keeps its old last run, so a dead scheduler looks exactly like a quiet
night in every row. `elixir:beat` does nothing except say the minute happened.

**One thing was not measured at all.** Nothing recorded a login: the users table carried
`is_first_login` and nothing else, so "which garage has not been here in months" was a question
the platform could not answer about its own dealers. `users.last_login_at` is written by the login
from now on. It is empty for everybody who has not signed in since, and the screen says exactly
that instead of showing them as never seen.

**And the 408 reports nobody ever read.** The "iets werkt niet"-button has been writing rows into
`anomaly` for years and nothing has ever read one. Four hundred messages that arrive nowhere are
worse than no button, because the button promises that somebody listens.

**The style job changes with it.** It now checks the files a branch *added*, not the ones it
changed. This pull request added one route line and one call in `LoginController`, and
`pint --diff` then asked for both legacy files to be reformatted from top to bottom inside a pull
request about something else. Pint judges a whole file, not a hunk, so "added" is the honest line
to draw in a repository where 864 files predate it.

Rules R P3-14.1 to R P3-14.10, twelve tests. What I deliberately left for later, once you have
looked at the screen: `api_log` is emptied after five days so nothing here reaches back further,
Modix and Nederland Mobiel keep no record of a run, and OpenAI counts nothing at all.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
params.title: Beheer > Werking: does the machine run
